correctness.rationale: Under the stated independent conditional-Poisson and fixed-spurious-positive model the all-negative probabilities are α^n under absence and α^n·product(q(vi)) under presence, where α=1−f and q(v)=1−p+p exp(−λ(v−c)). Their difference is Youden discrimination. g=−log q has g′>0 and g″<0; strict Jensen yields exactly the equal split, including the trivial n=1 case. For E=n g(B/n), direct differentiation gives E″=(B/n)^2 g″(B/n)/n<0, and log(1−exp(−E)) is increasing and strictly concave in E>0. Adding n log α preserves strict log-concavity, which orders secant slopes and makes strict neighbor wins globally decisive (one-sided at an endpoint). This does not assert unique maximizers at every intermediate budget; adjacent finite-budget ties can occur. At fixed count E increases strictly with B. I independently certified the four comparisons with exact rational alternating partial sums of exp(−x), rather than the frozen checker’s reciprocal positive sums. The four certified lower margins exceed 0.0003434316, 0.0011327059, 0.0044248467 and 0.0002921463 respectively; the scores therefore certify the asserted 5-to-4 reversal. For large B, Cn=α^n(1−β^n), β=1−p, and the sign of C(n+1)−Cn is the sign of (1−αβ)β^n−f. Its one crossing gives the ceiling formula with equality only at an integer threshold. The geometric upper bound α^n and the positive limit of J1 restrict all large-budget maximizers to a fixed finite set. At a tie k,k+1 the positive deficits have leading terms α^n n β^(n−1) p e^(λc) e^(−λB/n), so the smaller count approaches faster and wins eventually. The witness threshold is strictly between 3 and 4 by rational signs. As a check on the credited f=0 contrast, the continuous optimum maximizes g(v)/v, with derivative sign v g′−g decreasing strictly from positive at c to negative at infinity; its fixed v gives a count proportional to B, and the integer optimum differs by at most one. value.rationale: More water improves discrimination at each fixed count, but can strictly reduce the unique globally preferred count because a new assay incurs an additional false-alarm risk. The exact example establishes that this is a real optimization phenomenon rather than numerical error, and the limiting count and tie-break explain the saturation regime. The result is a useful idealized design benchmark with independent grabs and symmetric sensitivity/specificity weighting, not a field prescription or a claim about correlated occupancy or biological uncertainty.
